anf_compare.notes: Translated from the PG 77 Greek. No published English version was used for wording.

choices.why: The same word used of the candidate at the end of the previous section: blameless, open to no charge.

choices.english: who have been censured for their faults undergo separation
choices.why: Excommunication as a penance; πταίσματα are faults or lapses.
rejected: rebuked because of reproaches (drops the separation and misreads πταισμάτων)

choices.why: A state (they are catechumens), not an action in progress.

choices.english: let them not depart this life
choices.why: A prohibition in the imperative, kept as a command; τὰ ἀνθρώπινα is human life.
rejected: so that they may not depart (turns the command into a purpose clause)

choices.term: ὑμᾶς ἡ σὺν ἡμῖν ἐν κυρίῳ προσαγορεύει
choices.english: the brotherhood that is with us greets you in the Lord
choices.why: The subject is ἡ (ἀδελφότης) σὺν ἡμῖν; a standard closing greeting, not a Scripture citation.
rejected: you are joined to us in the Lord (1 Corinthians 1:10)

pass_a_gloss: For we shall keep (tēreō) in this way (houtō) both our own conscience (syneidos) pure (katharos) and the holy (hieros) and venerable (septos) liturgy (leitourgia) blameless (adiablētos). [Heading, marked E in the copy-text:] Concerning the catechumens (katēchoumenoi) and those repenting (metanoeō), if they should draw near (engizō) to the end (telos). And if some undergo (hypomenō) separation (chōrismos), having been censured (epitimaō) on account of faults (ptaisma), and then are about to die (teleutaō), being catechumens, let them be baptized (baptizō), and let them not depart (apodēmeō) from human things without a share (ametochos) of the grace (charis), that is (ēgoun) without communion (akoinōnētos); for this also seems (dokeō) to keep to (prosechō) the ordinances (thesmos) of the church. Greet (proseipon) the brotherhood (adelphotēs) beside you; the [brotherhood] with us addresses (prosagoreuō) you in the Lord.
pass_b_english: For in this way we shall keep both our own conscience pure and the holy and venerable liturgy beyond reproach.
On catechumens and penitents, if they draw near their end

If any who have been censured for their faults undergo separation, and then are about to die while they are still catechumens, let them be baptized; and let them not depart this life without a share in grace, that is, without communion. For this too seems to be in keeping with the ordinances of the Church.
Greet the brotherhood that is with you; the brotherhood that is with us greets you in the Lord.

reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Replaces a rejected machine draft of 2026-09-30 (backup kept in the Wave A backup folder). That draft added an opening ellipsis to a complete sentence, dropped οὕτω, rendered ἀδιάβλητον 'undefiled', fused the heading into the canon, left out χωρισμὸν ὑπομείνωσί, mistranslated πταισμάτων and κατηχούμενοι ὄντες, turned the command μὴ ἀποδημείτωσαν into a purpose clause, reversed δοκεῖ ... προσέχειν τοῖς θεσμοῖς, and garbled the closing greeting with an invented citation (1 Corinthians 1:10).
Retranslated clause by clause against the Greek: 'Τηρήσομεν γὰρ οὕτω καθαρὸν καὶ τὸ ἑαυτῶν συνειδὸς' = 'For in this way we shall keep both our own conscience pure'.
The heading printed 'Ε' in the copy-text is rendered without a numeral, since its number is uncertain after (α)-(γ). Page marker 284 is not rendered.
No Scripture quoted or alluded to in this section; the closing greeting is a standard formula.
